transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I’ve been having a hard time since we got this new operations manager. He keeps picking apart inspection procedures I’ve used for years, and I can’t seem to shut it off when I get home. I’m wound up, snapping at my husband, lying awake replaying meetings. Then at work I’m second-guessing routine quality calls I used to make without any trouble.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about things other than what’s happening with your new manager at work?
No, not really. It’s mostly the work situation with him that keeps going around in my head.
Has this stress been making it hard for you to do your job?

Yes. I’ve missed some internal deadlines, and I’ve been pulling back from meetings I’m supposed to be at. It’s showing in my work record. And at home, my husband and I have been arguing more—I’m not keeping up with our usual evening routines like I normally do.
Have you been feeling down or depressed since this started with your new manager?
I’ve been pretty down about it, yes. I feel wound up all the time, and it’s upsetting that I’m second-guessing things at work that used to come easily to me.
Did these problems start within 3 months of the new operations manager taking over?
Yes. I was doing fine before he came in. Within a few weeks of the procedure changes, it started getting to me, and by the second month I could tell it was affecting me outside of work too.
If this situation with your new manager were not happening, do you think these symptoms would still be a problem?

No, I don’t think so. Before he started changing and criticizing the procedures I’ve used for years, I was able to do my job and come home without carrying it all with me. This really feels tied to what’s been happening at work.
Since this started, have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed a clear loss of interest in things I usually enjoy.
Even on nights when work isn’t on your mind, do you still have trouble falling or staying asleep?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really paid attention to whether it happens on nights when work isn’t on my mind.
Since this started, have you felt down most of the day nearly every day?
I’m not sure I’d say down most of the day, nearly every day. I’ve been upset about the work situation, but I haven’t really tracked it that closely.
Since this started, have you been less interested in or able to enjoy the things you usually like?
I haven’t really noticed that, no. I’m still able to enjoy the things I usually like when I do them.
If the situation with your new manager were resolved, do you think these symptoms would go away?

I think they probably would, but the situation isn’t resolved yet. I still have to report to him and deal with the procedures he changed. I haven’t had a time when it was over and these problems just kept going on their own for months.
Since this started, have you been feeling nervous or on edge?
Yes. Ever since the new manager started questioning the inspection procedures, I’ve been pretty wound up. I keep replaying meetings and second-guessing routine quality calls.
Since this started, have you been feeling sad?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed feeling sad, exactly.
When you have trouble sleeping, is it because your mind is stuck on problems with your manager?
Yes. I lie there replaying what was said in meetings and worrying over the changes he’s making to the inspection procedures. I can’t seem to shut it off.
Would you say your reaction to the problems with your new manager feels much stronger than most people would have in the same situation?

Yes, I think so. I know people would be bothered by a new manager changing things, but I’m taking it home with me every day. I’m wound up, snapping at my husband, and second-guessing work I used to handle without much trouble.
Since this started, have you often felt hopeless?
I don’t think so. I’ve been upset and worried, but I wouldn’t say I’ve felt hopeless.
Have you lost your job because of this situation at work?
No, I haven’t lost my job. But my work record has taken a hit—I’ve missed internal deadlines and pulled back from meetings I’m supposed to attend.
Since this started, have you been crying more than usual?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t particularly noticed crying more than usual.
Since this started, have you been feeling depressed?

I wouldn’t say depressed exactly, but I’ve been really upset and on edge since the new manager started criticizing the procedures I’ve used for years. It follows me home, and I just can’t seem to shake it.
Since this started, have you been feeling tearful?
I don’t think so. I haven’t noticed myself being especially tearful.
